sections.text: Man reaches perfection by dedicating his actions to God, Who is the source of all being, and fills everything.
It is better to do ones own duty, however defective it may be, than to follow the duty of another, however well one may perform it. He who does his duty as his own nature reveals it, never sins.
सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत्।
The duty that of itself falls to ones lot should not be abandoned, though it may have its defects. All acts are marred by defects, as fire is obscured by smoke.

Chapter 18, Moksha Sannyasa Yoga. Yoga of Liberation through Renunciation. We have discussed what this chapter is all about. You can see it as a summary or the final recommendations. You can see it like a summary of a long report. Youre trying to make sense out of it without reading the whole thing.
If you just read a summary before the full report, you might hear different interpretations about whats right. Similarly here, if you just read chapter 18 by itself, it probably wont make any sense to you. But if you read the entire Bhagavad Gita from chapter one through 17 and then read chapter 18, it should make sense to you. So what we have discussed so far is in Bhagavad Gita, the recommendations are made for your betterment, for your growth, for your happiness in general.
We have realized that in this world there are people who are different from each other. But each one is striving for the one and the same goal, which is to achieve happiness. Not only just the happiness in a finite term, but infinite term. I want to get happiness which never ends. So we all learned who we are at this limited self, what is our identity, what when we identify with the supreme, and how can we remove this parallax between the limited self and unlimited self to achieve that infinite happiness. So this chapter now brings it back to our attention that what we have discussed.
So what we have discussed so far is working in this world is absolutely necessary. In this world you will not be able to stand still without acting anything because of our experiences, that anytime I get involved in something and there are conflicts and there are frictions, and therefore it creates unhappiness. Maybe I should stay away from all these things. But thats not the answer, because you just cannot stay without doing anything. So therefore understand what action is all about. You should not give up actions, but act in accordance with the advice in the Sastra, which says that there are actions which are forbidden.
It is not that you and I have to invent the will all over again every time. We have the wisdom of our ancestors, our civilization, our culture which tells you that stay away from this. This is not going to help you. Just like you tell a child, dont put finger in the fire, youre going to get burnt. Dont put finger in the electrical outlet, youll get shot. You dont have to try it out to see whether it works or not.
So the Nishiddha Karma are forbidden -- so that you dont get burnt, you dont get completely destroyed. Now what is left is Nityaattachment and you shall achieve your goal of getting happiness. Thats basically a simple advice in the beginning. But then the question occurs that we are all of different temperaments and we all have different goals.
We act in different fields. Is it really applied to all of us or only apply to the great evolved people who have understood all this philosophy of life? And Bhagavan come to the conclusion, a guideline that no. It applies to all of you. Whether you are at the top of the pyramid or at the bottom of the pyramid in the society. Therefore, we have discussed the four types of people.
This classification which we have just learned in previous verses says there are four types of people. They are defined by their own nature, their own gunas. It does not say that because you are a Brahmana, these gunas are yours. Rather, because you have these gunas, youll be considered a Brahmana. You should consider yourself a Kshatriya because you have the following gunas: bravery, valor, brightness, lordliness.
Not the other way around. Its not because you are a Kshatriya, you should have these qualities, but because you have these qualities, you are a Kshatriya. And similarly, because you have certain qualities, you are a Vaishya or a Shudra. It did not say that one class is more important than the other. He said its applicable to all of you.
The advice given in Bhagavad Gita, whether you are at the lowest rank, at the Shudra level or the Brahmin level, it all will apply to you. So last time somebody asked me, can you make a reference to the Purusha Sukta in Riga Veda. So in Purusha Sukta the same idea is explained. Purusha Sukta starts with Sahastra, Sirisa, Purushaha, Sahastraksha, Sahastrapad. This Purusha is envisioned, is the universal being. If the entire creation is one being, then how will you view it?
Or the sage who saw this universe as one being, he saw him as a being with thousands of eyes and thousands of legs and thousands of mouths. Very similar to what we have learnt in Bhagavad Gita in that vishwarupadas in chapter 11. So he said, this Purusha is everywhere. Sabhumim, Visvatovratva, atyatistha dash Angalam. Hes enveloping the entire universe and is spreading in all ten directions. We have discussed before eight cardinal directions.
Northwest, east, south, northwest, southwest, southeast and northeast. Then eight up and down, 10, hes extending in all 10 directions. And then the question asks, what about his limbs? Brahmano mukha Asita. The first time you hear this Brahmano, Ashya Mukha, Asith, Brahmanas are his mouth. This universal being in his self is envisioned as what coming out of his mouth is Brahmanas.
So Brahmana, the knowledge speech, what we see is Brahmana, Asya Mukham, Asith, Bahuhu, Rajanya, Kritaha. His arms are made up of Rajanya, Kshatriyas, Uru tadasyat, Vaishyah. His thighs are made up of Vaishyas and Padyam Shudrajaya and his feet are made up of Shudras. The shudras constitute his feet, Vaisyas constitute his thighs, Kshatriyas constitute his arms and Brahmanas his mouth. This being cannot be complete if any one of them. You remove the complete picture of the Supreme Being.
It cannot be complete if you just take the Brahmanas and say other three are not necessary. He is who he is because all four parts. And then it continues and says Nabya Asid Antariksha. His navel forms the space between the heaven and the earth. Sishnav dyo Samovar Tathaha, his head sustained in heaven. Padma Bhumir Disaha, your feet are sustaining the earth.
Nakshatra, Tatha, Lokan Akalbayan and his ears the directions. So basically this one single entity is viewed as encompassing every part of the society, every part of our universe. Brahmanas are his mouth, Kshatriyas are his hands, arms and Vaishyas are his thigh. And shudras are his feet. Hes supported by Shudras and Vaishyas. But it is part of the same entity.
So its not the intention of the writer of this Purushaktam to put anyone down or so. But basically saying this system just cannot function unless there are all four types of people at any given time, at any given place, in any given society. So therefore we have discussed in this that there are four types of people. You may fall in any one of them depending on your qualities. If you find your qualities to be of service, your Shudra and as we said, entire service sector now today can be part of Shudras. Because we are serving.
Serving is the nature of Shudras. Creating wealth is the nature of Vaishyas. If you put the Vaishyas where the Rajanya is supposed to be, that happens. What is happening in USA now? So Bhagawan said that each one has own quality. And when you try to mix each other without understanding, it may create issues and problems.
But if you understand yourself and where you stand, at least at your level -- this Bhagavad Gita is for self-unfoldment, for individual self-development. So the next four verses, from 45 through 48, are actually the essence of how to be successful. If we forget the entire message of Bhagavad Gita but understand these four verses, contemplate on them, and practice them, Bhagavan guarantees that you will be a happy person and a successful person. These verses are applicable to all four classes of people. Not just for the Brahmins, and not just for Kshatriyas or Vaishyas, but even Kshudras, all four of them.
If they can stick to this formula of success, then success is guaranteed. Thats basically what these four verses are all about. Verse 45, which we have seen, says: devoted to ones own duty, a man attains perfection. Perfection here should not be taken in the ordinary sense. It is the realization that now I have realized what my true self is. Whatever the field youre practicing, if you stay within your own nature, you will achieve perfection in that. If Im a sweeper, if I focus into it, Ill achieve perfection. I always wonder -- all these people who have a garbage collection company, I mean, at some point the guy had some interest in garbage collection, right? Before he became a big businessman with lots of trucks running around all over Richmond.
You cant suddenly get interested in garbage collection. I actually had a client one time with one of these recycling businesses. Just passing through his yard -- all junk all around it. Then you go to his office, which is air-conditioned, a nice little office, nice little conference room. But just going through that yard made me realize that this guy must really feel comfortable in this environment. Therefore, he can be a successful businessman trading in this recycling business.
Bhagavan said, wherever you feel comfortable, according to your own dharma. If you follow the actions. If you perform actions in your own field of interest. Sansiddhim Labate Naraha person gets success. Thats as simple as that. If I try to do something which is not my nature, I may get some success here and there.
But Ill never get full success. I tried developing some hotels and lost my shirt. But designing hotels I do very well. So after I lost all my investment, I said, let me go back to what I do best. Keep designing for other people. I can give advice to other people.
Where to build hotels, what is the right location, what will work, what will not work. I tried to do it myself. The Bhagavan said, if you stay within your realm of interest, of your own nature, success is guaranteed. You will achieve success. Swag karma nirataha Siddhim Yatha Vindha di tatsurana. But how that happens?
Bhagawan said, Ill tell you now how working in the field of your own interest, one can get. Siddhi -- perfection, success, expertise. And we find in this world all kinds of experts. Every time I come across a new challenge in my profession, something which I never heard about -- somebody says design something and it requires something so unique -- how do I figure this thing out?
And then I realize that there are experts even in disaster recovery. Suddenly you find that there are experts in this world who deal with that type of disaster which we have never thought about. How can you have experts in that field when the disaster only occurs once in a while? Because there are people who find their niche and they become experts because they pursue the field of their interest. So Arjuna asks, How do they do it? Bhagavan says, I will explain to you now. So the next three verses.
This simply says how you should view your own field of interest.

These verses form what calls the formula for success applicable to all people regardless of their station. Verse 46 reveals how work becomes worship: sva-karmana tam abhyarchya - by worshipping through ones own work, the one from whom all beings arise and by whom all this is pervaded, a person attains siddhi. This transforms every action into a sacred offering. The mechanic worships through perfect repairs; the teacher through patient instruction; the parent through loving care. No action is too mundane when offered to the Source. Verse 47 repeats the earlier teaching: better is ones own dharma, though imperfect, than anothers dharma well-performed. Svabhava-niyatam karma kurvan napnoti kilbisham - performing action determined by ones own nature, one incurs no sin. Verse 48 adds a crucial insight: sahajam karma - innate or natural work - should not be abandoned even if it has defects, because sarvarambha hi doshena - all undertakings are covered with defects as fire is covered by smoke. No work is perfect; waiting for perfect conditions means never acting. What is your sahajam karma - the work that naturally suits you? Today, release the perfectionism that prevents wholehearted engagement. Accept that your work will have defects (like smoke accompanies fire) and offer it anyway. The defects belong to the work; liberation belongs to the attitude. Practice this: before beginning your next task, consciously dedicate it to the Source from which your abilities arise. During the work, stay present rather than projecting to results. After completion, release it - let the outcome unfold without grasping.
